solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine cutting to make surgeon feel queasy

parts.note: to do a thing is to make it, as in do a drawing
a vet is a veterinary surgeon
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: A delicate operation so gruesome that even a surgeon goes green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgeon' points to a hospital, but an animal surgeon is meant; the definition is carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a woodworking joint of interlocking wedge-shaped cuts, which demands precise sawing.

clue.text: One missing from file, someone slacking?

indicators.note: something missing from a word has been taken out of it, so the letter for one leaves the file

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers on a subject
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An absent document hints that someone in the office is idling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser is a British informal word for an idler or layabout who avoids work.

clue.text: Shopkeeper from Devon traded close to Exeter

indicators.note: letters traded swap places with one another, so the county name is rearranged
the close of a word is its end, so this takes the final letter of the city

explanation.surface: A West Country shopkeeper doing business near Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traded' makes VENDO from DEVON, and 'close to' adds the R that ends Exeter. Devon is an English county; Exeter is its main city.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a seller, and a shopkeeper is one who sells goods.

clue.text: Presumably, seven green bottles left here

definitions.text: Presumably, seven green bottles left here

parts.words: Presumably, seven green bottles left here
parts.note: in the counting song Ten Green Bottles, seven left means three have fallen, and this clue sits in the grid at that very spot

explanation.surface: A nursery song's countdown, part way through.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten Green Bottles is a children's song in which bottles fall one at a time; with seven left, three are down. The clue is itself 3 Down, a self-referential joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both the clue's grid position and the tally of fallen bottles in the song.

clue.text: Simon's priest is suffering funny turns

indicators.note: a body that is suffering is in a bad way, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A clergyman named Simon is having strange dizzy spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny turns' looks like an illness, but means comic acts. 'suffering' rearranges all the letters of SIMONS PRIEST IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionists are comedians who mimic famous people, and their acts are funny turns on stage.

clue.text: Youth describes female objectively: a plump cutie

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the young one goes around the female

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in a cub scout or cub reporter
her is the object form of the female pronoun she

explanation.surface: A youngster gives a frank description of a chubby sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objectively' is grammar: the object case of 'she' is 'her'. 'describes' means draws round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is pictured in art as a chubby winged child, the very image of a plump cutie.

clue.text: Big-mouthed barrel-chested menace in post office

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is a synonym of hip

explanation.surface: A loud, burly thug causing trouble at the post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but the word for trendy, HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus has a huge gaping mouth and a barrel body, and is one of Africa's most dangerous animals.

clue.text: Sally returned umbrella Sir Percival carries around

indicators.note: turned around, the concealed letters are read in the opposite direction
the phrase carries the answer within it, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally hands back an umbrella that a knight takes round with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' finds LASIRPER spanning umbreLLA SIR PERcival, and 'around' turns it to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attack, and one sent back in response is a retaliation.

clue.text: You must carry trembling bride's primrose

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece carries the upper one on top of it, so the pronoun comes last
something trembling shakes about, so the letters of the word are jumbled

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A nervous bride holds a posy of primroses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the lower piece carries the upper one, so the pronoun goes at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird's-eye primrose is a small pink wild species of the primula family.

clue.text: Drink deal in pubs gets director on a bicycle

parts.note: a drop is a small drink, as in a drop of whisky
to handle goods is to deal in them
bars are pubs or drinking places

explanation.surface: A pub drinks deal draws in a passing cyclist with a film career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' looks like a film-maker but means the thing that steers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop handlebars curve downwards on a racing bike, and the rider steers the machine with them.

clue.text: Taps run when turned, one gets hot

indicators.note: turned here means altered in arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Turn the taps and the water warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: The hot taps are a decoy: 'when turned' rearranges TAPSRUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny spot that becomes unusually warm.

clue.text: Penny's in Harvester, paste rolls again?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the coin's letter goes within the harvester

parts.note: a reaper is a harvester of grain
P is the abbreviation for penny, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A coin dropped into a harvesting machine, then something about pasting rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' are rolls of wallpaper; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaper a room is to hang fresh wallpaper, pasting the rolls up a second time.

clue.text: Take flight to away match

definitions.meaning: to go away in order to be matched, that is wed

explanation.surface: A football fan flies off to watch the team play away.
explanation.definitionFit: Elopers run away together to marry in secret, a flight that ends in a match.

clue.text: Centre for pseuds and fakes sounds charming

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the two central ones

parts.note: phonies are fakes or frauds

explanation.surface: A refuge for pretentious frauds is a delightful place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre for' takes EU from the middle of pseuds.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphonies are pleasing combinations of sounds, so they are charming sounds.

clue.text: Police like a spreadsheet, perhaps on criminals unknown

indicators.note: on means the spreadsheet word is placed on, after, the criminals, so it comes second

parts.note: cons, short for convicts, are criminals
a spreadsheet is one example of data set out tabular, in rows and columns
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Detectives tracking lawbreakers on a spreadsheet with gaps in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A constabulary is a police force, especially a regional one in Britain.

clue.text: Loose dog journalist found after sunset, out of bounds

indicators.note: found after means these pieces follow the trimmed word
with its bounds, the outer letters, taken off, only the interior of the word remains

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A stray dog and a reporter wander out at dusk into forbidden ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of bounds' looks like part of the scene but strips the ends from sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsecured is not fastened down, so it is loose.

clue.text: Turning up in Channel Islands, French tennis player's unconvinced

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reverses the letters, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: Jo-Wilfried Tsonga is a French tennis player

explanation.surface: A French tennis star appears in Jersey or Guernsey and has doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses CI and TSONGA together. The Channel Islands are British islands off France.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence is unknown, being unconvinced either way.

clue.text: There on vacation, note English everywhere

parts.note: a ten is a ten-pound banknote
rife means widespread, found everywhere

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's note that English is spoken all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like an emptying signal but is part of the definition; 'There' is a place one goes on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is a Spanish island in the Canaries and a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Fire engine needs doggers to move

indicators.note: letters that need to move must change position, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fire engine wants the people in the way to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges NEEDSDOGGERS. Green Goddesses were old British army fire engines brought out during firefighters' strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Goddess was the nickname of the green-painted emergency fire engines of Britain's civil defence.

clue.text: Work for one or two minutes on a tattoo concealing it

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer, which is found within its consecutive letters

explanation.surface: A tattoo job lasting a minute or two that hides something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing it' finds the answer across minuteS ON A TAttoo. 'one or two' joins 'Work for', not 'minutes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition for one instrument or for a solo instrument with piano.

clue.text: Empty seat intended for you and me standing

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: something aimed at a target is intended for it, giving at
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: A vacant seat reserved for the two of us, so we must stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves ST from seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means social standing, one's rank or position.

clue.text: Factory worker's first to offer musical theatre in recession

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter
receding means going backwards, so these words are reversed

parts.note: Evita is a musical
rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A factory hand finally gets to put on a show while the economy shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reverses EVITAREP to PERATIVE, after O from offer.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker who runs machines in a factory.

clue.text: Collection of 8 diagrams finally finished? Not quite

indicators.note: finished points at the word's end, the part that goes missing here
not quite the whole word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A long-awaited book of diagrams is very nearly done.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' is 8 Down, BIRD'S-EYE: maps are bird's-eye diagrams. 'Not quite' cuts the T from AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, which are bird's-eye views of land.

clue.text: Conservative boor in power

parts.note: a lout is a boor

explanation.surface: An uncouth Tory politician holding office.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means influence, the power to get things done.

clue.text: One must have siblings allowed on holiday

indicators.note: on means one piece follows the other, so the permission comes after the outing

parts.note: a trip is a holiday
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A rule that a child may travel only with brothers and sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at one birth, so always has two siblings.

clue.text: Point aft of sailor right alongside

indicators.note: aft means behind, so the compass point comes after the other pieces

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A navigational instruction aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side, level with something.

clue.text: Run through finish line painted on the grass

indicators.note: running through something goes inside it

parts.note: to cease is to finish
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sprinter dashes over the finishing line on a grass track.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is cricket's white line marking where a batter is safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the crease is a white line marked on the pitch's turf.

clue.text: Bangers exploding scared us

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Fireworks going off frightened us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangers' are fireworks in the surface, but British slang for old cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for an old, battered car, typical of the secondhand trade.
